text:
ranjit: Quick follow-up from the warmup RFC thread — thinking about an "eviction-aware prefix" safeguard for safetensors warmup. Idea: attach a small "prefix_hotness" hint to shards so prefetch/warmup protects KV cache for the first N tokens of a request. Tradeoffs?

alexa: how does the hint travel? included in model manifest, sidecar metadata, or inferred at runtime?

morgan: we have per-shard static priority today, but prefix patterns are dynamic per-request. need a dynamic hint + aging.

benji: tradeoffs: protecting prefixes reduces cold-start latency for interactive sessions but increases resident memory for long-lived pods. Also complicates eviction heuristics.

ops-sre: SLA angle — we need a bounded memory policy. can't let soft reserves cause unbounded growth under load. any ideas on caps? :eyes: 

ranjit: proposal sketch: (1) manifest carries optional `prefix_hotness` per-shard (int 0-10) and `prefix_size_est` in bytes; (2) runtime exposes `reserve_prefix(session_id, shard_id, bytes)` which creates a soft-reserve entry in KV cache metadata; (3) soft-reserves are best-effort and subject to global cap; on pressure we reclaim from oldest sessions first. Telemetry to verify efficacy.

alexa: can you paste a minimal manifest snippet?

ranjit: ```json
{
  "shard_id": "m-0001",
  "format": "safetensors",
  "prefix_hotness": 7,
  "prefix_size_est": 32768
}
```

morgan: how does this interact with mmap-backed safetensors and shared-file descriptors? if multiple workers mmap same file, soft-reserve is per-process metadata only. evictions need coordination.

benji: agreed. two modes: "local-reserve" (fast, per-process) and "coordinated-reserve" (via shared kernel or memtable + HA lease). Start with local-reserve + conservative caps; add coordinated later.

ops-sre: suggest global limits: `max_prefix_reserve_per_node` and `max_prefix_reserve_per_model` — enforce with admission control on request start. That way we bound worst-case. Also emit rejection metric so clients can fallback.

ranjit: fallback policies: (a) if reserve denied -> warmup continues but deprioritized (no KV protection), (b) if eviction happens mid-request -> fallback to smaller model variant or server-side truncation of prefix cache. We should prefer model-variant fallback because it preserves tail latency.

alexa: metrics we should track: `ml.prefetch.prefix_hit_rate`, `ml.prefetch.prefix_eviction_rate`, `ml.kv.soft_reserve_current_bytes`, `ml.kv.soft_reserve_reclaimed_count`. Also tag by model, shard, and route.

benji: implementation note: keep the reserve metadata compact (8 bytes/shard reservation entry) and store in the existing shard-index. Avoid touching the safetensors on-disk format. No file-format churn if manifest is sidecar JSON.

morgan: load-path compatibility: for manifest-less checkpoints (S3 lists), we can derive `prefix_size_est` heuristically from embedding layer dims or prompt templates. But prefer opt-in manifest to avoid bad guesses.

ranjit: experiments to run: A/B with 10k interactive sessions, compare cold-token latency and memory delta for `max_prefix_reserve_per_node` = {32MB, 64MB, 128MB}. We'll also test `prefix_hotness` thresholds 3/7/9.

ops-sre: add a canary that flips on `coordinated-reserve` for one pool only. infra-bot will create the feature flag.

infra-bot: Feature flag `eviction_prefix_reserve` created in canary namespace `ml-canary-3`. Canary rollout scheduled for tomorrow 04:00 UTC.

alexa: one more question — should warmup call `reserve_prefix` at request start or only when it sees an actual prefix length > 0? if at start, we might reserve for many short queries.

ranjit: prefer lazy: reserve when warmup sees prefix tokens > threshold (e.g., 32). That avoids spurious reserves for single-token calls. Document default thresholds and make route-configurable.

benji: ok. I'll draft a small RFC addendum with API surface, config knobs, and metric names. Will add a pseudo-code sketch for eviction choice logic.

morgan: +1. also include a short test harness to simulate shared-mmap behavior (forked workers) so we can observe cross-process eviction races.

ranjit: thanks everyone — action items: benji will write addendum, ops-sre to propose the admission-control knobs, morgan to build simulation, alexa to add telemetry dashboard queries. We'll reconvene after canary results. :thumbsup:
